description: Stands in for the MetaModule hardware inside a Rack patch: its knobs and jacks represent the ones on the hardware, and the patch around it is saved as a file the hardware can play

params.text: Stands for one of the hardware's six large knobs; drag from the small circle beside it onto any knob in the patch and that knob then follows this one
Stands for one of the hardware's six small knobs; drag from the small circle beside it onto any knob in the patch and that knob then follows this one
Writes the patch out as a MetaModule .yml patch file, using the name typed into the panel's text field
Sends the patch file over the network to the address set on the menu

inputs.text: Marks the cable that feeds one of the hardware's eight output jacks; in Rack this jack passes no signal

outputs.text: Marks where one of the hardware's six input jacks arrives in the patch; in Rack this jack passes no signal
Marks where one of the hardware's two gate input jacks arrives in the patch; in Rack this jack passes no signal

notes: The module is inert in Rack: nothing patched into it is heard and nothing comes out. Its jacks record which cables belong to which hardware jack.
A knob does nothing until it is mapped: drag from the coloured circle beside it onto a knob anywhere in the patch. One hub knob can drive several knobs.
The two text fields at the top are the patch name and the patch description, which are written into the saved file.
The row of small buttons beside the knobs chooses which knob set is in use, so one panel of knobs can hold several sets of mappings.
menu: Include modules from: All, Left & Right Only, Right Only, Left Only, Connected — chooses which modules in the rack are gathered into the saved patch
Set Wi-Fi Expander address — opens a box for the network address a sent patch goes to
Wi-Fi sends to: Internal, USB, Card — chooses which of the hardware's drives a sent patch is written to
Jack Aliases — gives each of the sixteen panel jacks a name of your own, which the hardware then shows
Mapped Knob Sets — chooses which knob set is in use, and names it
Module Aliases — renames the modules in the patch and gives them colours, for the hardware's own display
Use stoermelder GLUE labels for module aliases — takes module names from stoermelder GLUE labels in the patch rather than from the ones set here
Suggested sample rate — records a sample rate in the patch file for the hardware to use
Suggested block size — records an audio block size in the patch file for the hardware to use
Use built-in MIDI — records that the patch expects the hardware's own MIDI rather than Rack's
Use RackCore MIDI — records that the patch expects Rack's Core MIDI modules rather than the hardware's
Automatically map AudioInterface to panel outs — connects a Rack audio module's channels to the hub's output jacks without patching them by hand
